name: Embrace the Unknown — Méridien Audio's Frontier Bet
description: A four-round, advanced innovation-strategy simulation set inside Méridien Audio SAS, a French premium-audio maker (Lyon, EUR 240M revenue, 12% operating margin, 620 employees). At a Berlin trade show a venture-backed entrant launches an AI audio platform that licenses personalisation software to any hardware maker — sidestepping Méridien's entire premium-device thesis. Sell-through is flat, not falling: this is genuine Knightian uncertainty, not measurable risk, and there is no burning platform — only a fog. As Innovation Lead you have a discretionary war chest of EUR 6 million and a 9-month runway before FY2027 commitments lock, against an estimated EUR 40M full pivot the board will never approve on a hunch. Built on Nathan & Susannah Furr's 'The Upside of Uncertainty' (2022), the simulation runs the real arc across four rounds: (1) reframe the threat — distinguish risk from uncertainty and convert an ambiguous threat into the most promising opportunity framing with its make-or-break assumption named; (2) buy information cheaply — design a portfolio of low-cost, fast probes (a software pilot, an open-profile retailer trial, a fake-door D2C test, an acqui-hire) scored on belief-change-per-euro and cheap enough to walk away from; (3) read mixed, partly contradictory evidence and update beliefs honestly rather than confirming the reframe you fell in love with; and (4) decide WHEN and WHETHER to commit, at what size and with what staging, weighing option erosion and talent loss against a premature oversized bet. The math rewards reframing, disciplined probing and well-timed staged commitment, and punishes the five classic errors: waiting for certainty, premature full commitment, false precision (inventing probabilities for genuine uncertainty), sunk-cost probes too expensive to abandon, and probe paralysis past the point of diminishing learning. Final KPIs track Uncertainty Resolved, Option Value, Conviction Quality and the remaining Runway (EUR and months).

Your Decisions This Round

Willingness to be proven wrong: 60
Uncertainty still unresolved: 50
Facilitator (playing the board chair)
Uncertainty is not resolved by waiting — the data you want will arrive the same week the opportunity closes. Don't force a false probability onto a fog, and don't bet €40M on a trade show and one email. Buy information cheaply, update honestly, and commit when enough uncertainty is resolved and before the window shuts. What can you learn for €200,000 this month?
